payload.meta_description: Plan a destination wedding in Greece from Australia: where to marry, which months, the legal route, sourced budget figures and getting your guests there.
payload.excerpt: The Australian couple's planning overview for a wedding in Greece: islands or mainland, the months, the legal route in brief, Santorini budget figures, guest travel and an 18-month timeline.
secondary_keywords: getting married in greece from australia
payload.author: TBC (open item AUTHOR)
key_takeaways: Choose the island by guest count and guest travel before you choose the view: our venues guide notes that venues in Crete and on the Athens Riviera publish space for several hundred guests, and the mainland needs no ferry.

The Australian Embassy in Athens says Greek municipal and religious bodies require a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage from each non-Greek partner, and Smartraveller says a marriage valid in Greece is in most cases legally recognised in Australia, although it cannot be registered here.
Our Santorini cost breakdown (November 2026) puts a standard wedding of 50 to 80 guests at EUR 30,000 to EUR 55,000; other islands and the mainland price differently.

Smartraveller warns that summer heatwaves are frequent, that wildfires occur from June to September and that ferries can be delayed or cancelled in strong winds, so build in a spare day and a covered alternative.
Smartraveller says Australian guests can visit the Schengen area without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, with fingerprints and a photo taken under the EU Entry/Exit System on arrival.

faq.q: How much does a destination wedding in Greece cost?
faq.a: It depends on the island and your guest count. For Santorini, our cost breakdown (November 2026) gives EUR 4,000 for an elopement to EUR 55,000 or more, depending on guest count and style. Other islands and the mainland price differently, so ask for itemised quotes in euros.

faq.q: Is a wedding in Greece legally recognised in Australia?
faq.a: In most cases, yes. Smartraveller says an overseas marriage is legally recognised in Australia if it was valid where it happened and would have been valid under Australian law. You cannot register it in Australia, and your Greek marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage.

faq.q: What is the best month for a wedding in Greece?
faq.a: There is no single answer: it depends on the island, how much heat your guests can manage and, for an Orthodox wedding, the church calendar. Our best-time guide sets out each month, island by island. Smartraveller warns that summer heatwaves are frequent and that wildfires occur from June to September.

faq.q: Can we marry legally in Australia and have a symbolic ceremony in Greece?
faq.a: Yes. You complete the legal marriage at home under Australian rules, then hold a symbolic ceremony in Greece with no legal effect there. The Attorney-General's Department says an Australian-authorised celebrant cannot perform a marriage overseas, so on this route the legal ceremony happens in Australia before you fly.

faq.q: Do our guests need a visa to attend a wedding in Greece?
faq.a: Not for a short stay on an Australian passport. Smartraveller says Australians can travel to the Schengen area without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Guests have fingerprints and a photo taken under the EU Entry/Exit System on arrival, which is free, and ETIAS has no confirmed start date. Guests on other passports should check their own rules.
